## Row {height=86%}

```{r}
#| title: "Forecast for the next delivery day, with recent actual prices (EUR/MWh)"
p <- plot_ly() |>
  add_lines(data = today_act, x = ~hour, y = ~actual,
            name = paste("Actual", format(latest - 1, "%a %d %b"), "(day before)"),
            line = list(color = grey, width = 2, dash = "dot"),
            hovertemplate = paste0("%{y:.1f} €/MWh<extra>", format(latest - 1, "%a %d %b"), "</extra>")) |>
  add_lines(data = week_act, x = ~hour, y = ~actual,
            name = paste("Actual", format(latest - 7, "%a %d %b"), "(same weekday last week)"),
            line = list(color = "#cfc6bb", width = 2, dash = "dash"),
            hovertemplate = paste0("%{y:.1f} €/MWh<extra>", format(latest - 7, "%a %d %b"), "</extra>"))

# naive left out
fc_models <- setdiff(models, "naive_mix")
fc_models <- c(main, setdiff(fc_models, main))   # open on main model

for (m in fc_models) {
  d <- tomorrow |> select(hour, f = all_of(m)) |> left_join(fan_wide(m), by = "hour") |>
    mutate(range90 = ifelse(is.na(q0.05), "", sprintf(", 90%%: %.0f to %.0f", q0.05, q0.95)))
  col <- model_colors[[m]]
  vis <- m == fc_models[1]
  p <- p |>
    add_lines(data = d, x = ~hour, y = ~q0.05, line = list(width = 0), showlegend = FALSE,
              visible = vis, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
    add_lines(data = d, x = ~hour, y = ~q0.95, line = list(width = 0), fill = "tonexty",
              fillcolor = rgba(col, 0.12), name = paste0("90% range, ", q_low(q_method(m))),
              visible = vis, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
    add_lines(data = d, x = ~hour, y = ~q0.25, line = list(width = 0), showlegend = FALSE,
              visible = vis, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
    add_lines(data = d, x = ~hour, y = ~q0.75, line = list(width = 0), fill = "tonexty",
              fillcolor = rgba(col, 0.25), name = "50% range",
              visible = vis, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
    add_lines(data = d, x = ~hour, y = ~f, text = ~range90,
              name = paste0(model_labels[[m]], " forecast ", format(latest, "%a %d %b"),
                            ", made ", format(made_dk, "%a %d %b %H:%M")),
              visible = vis,
              line = list(color = col, width = 3),
              hovertemplate = paste0("%{y:.1f} €/MWh%{text}<extra>", model_labels[[m]], "</extra>"))
}

p |> chart_layout(fc_models, xtitle = "Hour (Danish time)", n_fixed = 2, per_model = 5) |> layout(xaxis = list(dtick = 3))
```

## Row {height=56%}

```{r}
#| title: "Live forecasts vs actual prices, last 30 days (EUR/MWh)"
if (nrow(scored) == 0) {
  cat("The track record starts once the first forecast day has passed.")
} else {
  sc <- scored |> mutate(time = as_datetime(date, tz = "Europe/Copenhagen") + hours(hour))

  p2 <- plot_ly(sc, x = ~time) |>
    add_lines(y = ~actual, name = "Actual",
              line = list(color = ink, width = 1.5),
              hovertemplate = "%{y:.1f} €/MWh<extra>Actual</extra>")

  for (m in models) {
    p2 <- p2 |>
      add_lines(y = sc[[m]], name = model_labels[[m]],
                visible = (m == models[1]),
                line = list(color = model_colors[[m]], width = 1.5),
                hovertemplate = paste0("%{y:.1f} €/MWh<extra>", model_labels[[m]], "</extra>"))
  }

  p2 |> chart_layout(models)
}
```

## Row {height=30%}

```{r}
#| title: "Accuracy by model, last 30 days"
acc_live <- bind_rows(lapply(models, \(m) {
  s <- scored[!is.na(scored[[m]]), ]
  if (nrow(s) == 0) return(NULL)
  tibble(Model            = model_labels[[m]],
         `Days tracked`   = n_distinct(s$date),
         `MAE (€/MWh)`    = mean(abs(s$actual - s[[m]])),
         `RMSE (€/MWh)`   = sqrt(mean((s$actual - s[[m]])^2)))
}))
if (nrow(acc_live) > 0) {
  acc_live |> arrange(`MAE (€/MWh)`) |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)
} else {
  cat("Starts once a forecast day of these models has passed.")
}
```

::: {.card}
Every forecast here was saved before the auction and never changed. Want to see the backtest? [Click here](backtest.html).

## Row {height=440px}

```{r}
#| title: "Live days: battery revenue and its 95% floor (€)"
if (is.null(risk_live) || nrow(risk_live) == 0) {
  cat("Starts after the first live day.")
} else {
  risk_live |>
    transmute(Day = format(as_date(date), "%a %d %b %Y"), `Planned` = eur(planned), Expected = eur(expected),
              `95% floor` = eur(floor), Revenue = eur(realized), `Below the floor` = ifelse(miss, "yes", "")) |>
    knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrl")
}
```

::: {.card title="How it works"}

The battery's plan for tomorrow is made on the ensemble forecast before the auction. With the plan fixed,
its revenue is the plan times the prices, so the risk comes from the forecast errors in the hours it
trades. The scenarios are the 24-hour errors of past days, kept whole so the hours stay correlated, run
through tomorrow's plan, with filtered historical simulation (each past day's errors scaled by an EWMA of
the forecast errors before it, λ = 0.94, up to 250 days). VaR is how far below the expected revenue the
worst day in 20 falls; ES is the average shortfall on those days.

The method was chosen in a backtest of four ways to build the scenarios. Want to see the backtest? [Click here](backtest.html).

:::

# Method {scrolling="true"}

## Row {height=260px}

::: {.card title="Challengers: tested live before they can replace the ensemble"}

```{r}
#| output: asis
if (!is.null(chall) && nrow(chall) > 0) {
  arrow <- function(a, b) ifelse(is.na(a), "\u2013", sprintf("%.1f \u2192 %.1f", a, b))
  ch_tab <- chall |>
    transmute(Challenger      = label,
              `Backtest MAE`  = arrow(backtest_mae_champion, backtest_mae_challenger),
              `Backtest p`    = ifelse(is.na(backtest_p), "\u2013", p_tab(backtest_p)),
              `Live days`     = live_days,
              `Live MAE`      = arrow(live_mae_champion, live_mae_challenger),
              `Live p (Holm)` = ifelse(is.na(live_p_holm), "\u2013", p_tab(live_p_holm)),
              Status          = status)
  if (nrow(chall) == 1) names(ch_tab)[names(ch_tab) == "Live p (Holm)"] <- "Live p"
  cat(knitr::kable(ch_tab, format = "html", align = "lrrrrrl",
                   table.attr = 'class="table table-sm table-striped small"'))
  cat("\n\nMAE: ensemble \u2192 challenger, €/MWh. ", chall_txt, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

:::

## Row {height=920px}

::: {.card title="How it works"}

**Target.** Since 1 October 2025 the auction sets a price for every quarter-hour; the forecasts are for
the hourly average of the four quarters.

**Models.** All use the DK1 prices from D-1, D-2, D-3 and D-7, neighbour prices (DE, DK2, NO2,
SE3, SE4) from D-1, holidays, and weather forecasts made 48 hours ahead for DK1 and Germany
([Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com): wind speed at 100 m through a simple power curve at three wind
areas in DK1 and five in Germany, and solar radiation at three solar areas in each), so everything is
known before the noon auction. Energinet's own wind and solar forecasts are published at 18:00, after
the auction, so they are only in the study on the backtest page. All are re-estimated every day on the
previous two years (the weather archive starts in March 2024, so the window is shorter until March
2026), on prices transformed with asinh((p − median) / MAD).

**BMT-X**, boosting with multiple testing (Kapetanios, Sarafidis & Ventouri), the method from my
master's thesis: variables are added one at a time, each the most significant given the ones already
in, until none passes a multiple-testing threshold; then OLS. One model per hour.

**LEAR-X** (after Lago 2021): one LASSO per hour on the same variables, lambda by BIC.

**XGBoost-X**: boosted trees, one model for all hours. Depth and rounds picked on `r if (!is.null(xgb_tun)) xgb_tun$n_days[1] else ""` days before the
test period and kept fixed. `r xgb_txt`

**Ensemble:** the plain average of BMT-X, LEAR-X and XGBoost-X.

**Benchmark:** the weekly naive: last week's prices on Mondays, Saturdays and Sundays, yesterday's on
other days. rMAE = MAE relative to it.

**Tests:** best model vs each other model. DM = Diebold-Mariano on the daily average absolute error,
with a Newey-West variance over one week of lags because good and bad days come in runs (and the HLN
correction), GW = Giacomini-White, hours = how many of the 24 hours it is significantly better /
worse (Holm). The model confidence set (Hansen, Lunde & Nason, 10%, 7-day block bootstrap) keeps the
models that can't be told apart from the best one.

**Bias:** mean error above 0 = too low on average; Mincer-Zarnowitz slope above 1 = moves too little
(MZ p tests intercept 0 and slope 1, Newey-West). Two corrections are tested, both from the last `r k_bias`
days only: adding the median error, and a + b × forecast from the Mincer-Zarnowitz regression
(Theil's optimal linear correction).

**Ranges:** quantiles from 5% to 95% from the last `r k_q` days' errors of each model, per hour, in three
ways: the plain error quantiles; the same scaled by last week's volatility; and adaptive (after Gibbs &
Candès 2021), which also nudges the quantile levels each day after it sees whether the prices fell
below them. Scored with the pinball loss (average over the `r length(taus)` levels, lower is better). Calibration
error = average distance between the level and the share of prices below it. Calibration first, then
sharpness (Gneiting, Balabdaoui & Raftery 2007): the method used has the lowest pinball loss among
those whose 50% and 90% ranges are not significantly off target (Newey-West t test on the daily coverage).
Skill vs naive = how much lower the pinball loss is than the same method on the weekly naive forecast.
The chance of a negative price is read off the same quantiles and scored with the Brier score.

**Challengers:** changes that could replace the ensemble (now the bias correction above) run next to
it live first, with a decision rule fixed in advance (see the Challengers card). ENTSO-E's day-ahead load forecasts for DK1 and Germany are downloaded too, but once
German weather is in the models they add nothing, so they aren't used.

**Live:** each forecast is made at about 10:15 Danish time the day before, saved with the time it
was made, and never changed. After the noon auction nothing is saved.
German weather is used from the forecast for 14 October 2026. The live days before that were made
without it.

**Backtest:** accuracy tables, tests, ranges, the variables study and the battery backtest are on the [backtest page](backtest.html).

**Data:** [Energi Data Service](https://www.energidataservice.dk) (Energinet).<br>
**Code:** [github.com/jacobazu/dk1-price-forecasting](https://github.com/jacobazu/dk1-price-forecasting)<br>
**Last updated:** `r format(with_tz(Sys.time(), "Europe/Copenhagen"), "%d %B %Y, %H:%M")` (Danish time)

:::
